acceptance_criteria.criterion: `Parser::parse_charset()` uses `$el instanceof Node` instead of `!empty($el)` to resolve PHPStan type error at line 299
`composer analyze` no longer reports the two real type errors (only `missingType.iterableValue` warnings remain)
All 274+ tests continue to pass after the PHPStan fixes

summary: Fixed two PHPStan type errors: (1) Changed `!empty($el)` to `$el instanceof Node` in Parser::parse_charset() at line 298, eliminating the `property.nonObject` error (cannot access $content on array|Node). (2) Added `@property-read string $plaintext` to the Node class docblock, eliminating the unknown-property error. Also added `@property mixed $content` to Node's docblock to address the secondary `property.notFound` error at line 299 that surfaced after the instanceof narrowing. PHPStan now reports no `property.notFound` or `property.nonObject` errors — only the pre-existing `missingType.iterableValue`, `foreach.emptyArray`, `parameterByRef.type`, and `isset.offset` errors remain. All 275 tests pass."

comments.note: Adding `$el instanceof Node` correctly narrowed the type, but exposed a secondary PHPStan error `property.notFound` on $el->content (a dynamic attribute via __get). Fixed by adding `@property mixed $content` to Node docblock. This pattern (annotating commonly-accessed HTML attributes) may need to be extended if PHPStan errors surface for other dynamic attributes like $href, $src, $type, etc.

Zero failures or errors. The PHPStan fixes in WP-004 (instanceof narrowing in Parser.php and docblock annotations in Node.php) are purely type-level changes that carry no runtime behaviour change, so the full passing test suite confirms no regressions were introduced. comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. The PHPStan fixes are docblock/type-narrowing only; no runtime logic was altered, so no risk of test regressions.

summary: Code review PASS for WP-004 (Static Analysis Fixes). Two files verified: (1) Parser.php — `parse_charset()` at line 298 uses `if ($el instanceof Node)` to guard access to `$el->content`. This is the correct and idiomatic PHPStan type-narrowing idiom for `array|Node` union returns from `find()`. The guard eliminates the `property.nonObject` error cleanly without widening the type or suppressing the analysis. The `$fullvalue` variable is then extracted from `$el->content` (which is handled by Node's `__get`) inside the narrowed scope. The surrounding logic (charset fallback cascade to `mb_detect_encoding`, then to `UTF-8`) is unchanged and correct. (2) Node.php — The class docblock now contains two `@property` annotations: `@property-read string $plaintext` (delegates to `text()`, correctly marked read-only since there is no corresponding setter path for this virtual property) and `@property mixed $content` (marks the dynamic HTML attribute accessible via `__get`/`__set`). Both annotations are correctly formatted PHPDoc and are positioned before the class declaration. The `@property-read` annotation correctly matches the read-only nature of `$plaintext`, and `@property mixed $content` uses `mixed` appropriately since HTML attribute values can be string, null, or bool depending on the node. No runtime behaviour was altered — these are purely static-analysis metadata changes.

comments.note: Parser::parse_charset(): The instanceof guard is at line 298 which matches the AC specification exactly. The `!empty($el)` form that was replaced would have been truthy for both an array and a non-null Node object, so PHPStan could not narrow the type. The `instanceof Node` form is strictly more correct because it simultaneously establishes the type and excludes the empty-array case.

Node.php docblock: The addition of `@property mixed $content` alongside `@property-read string $plaintext` is a targeted, minimal fix. A broader improvement (annotating `$href`, `$src`, `$type`, `$class`, `$id`, etc.) would eliminate more dynamic-property PHPStan noise, but is correctly deferred — adding all common attributes to the docblock would be a separate maintenance task and does not affect the correctness of this fix.
No observations — code is clean and consistent. The two changes are purely type-level metadata; zero risk of runtime regression.
